reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: Characterised by craniosynostosis (often bicoronal), midface hypoplasia and, distinctively, radiohumeral or radioulnar synostosis limiting elbow movement
Two aetiologies exist: a recessive form from cytochrome P450 oxidoreductase (POR) deficiency, and cases associated with FGFR2 mutations
The POR-deficiency form causes a disorder of steroidogenesis, so ambiguous genitalia and abnormal steroid profiles can occur, and it may be associated with maternal virilisation in pregnancy
Fluconazole exposure in pregnancy produces a phenocopy, so a medication history is important
Additional features include arachnodactyly, joint contractures, femoral bowing and fractures, and choanal atresia or stenosis
Choanal atresia and midface hypoplasia together create a substantial neonatal airway risk
Distinguishing POR deficiency is critical because it requires assessment of adrenal steroid synthesis and potential steroid support
Care is multidisciplinary, combining craniofacial surgery, orthopaedic management and endocrine evaluation
reference.pathophysiology: Antley-Bixler syndrome is genetically heterogeneous. The recessive form is caused by deficiency of cytochrome P450 oxidoreductase (POR), the electron-donor enzyme required by multiple microsomal cytochrome P450 enzymes, including those of steroid and sterol synthesis; impaired activity disrupts steroidogenesis (causing genital and hormonal abnormalities) and sterol-dependent developmental signalling, producing the skeletal malformations. Other cases arise from activating FGFR2 mutations that cause premature suture fusion. Prenatal exposure to certain azole antifungals inhibiting sterol synthesis can mimic the skeletal phenotype.
additionalDifferentials: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (for the steroidogenic abnormality)
additionalInvestigations: Molecular testing of POR and FGFR2 to establish the underlying cause
Adrenal and sex-steroid profiling, including precursors, to detect disordered steroidogenesis
Three-dimensional cranial CT to define suture fusion
Skeletal survey to document radiohumeral synostosis, bowing and fractures
Airway and choanal assessment, including nasal endoscopy or imaging for choanal atresia
Detailed maternal medication history focused on antifungal exposure in pregnancy
redFlags: Neonatal airway obstruction from choanal atresia with midface hypoplasia
Adrenal insufficiency or salt-wasting crisis in the POR-deficiency form
Ambiguous genitalia requiring urgent endocrine and multidisciplinary assessment
reference.prognosis: Neonatal outcome is dominated by airway and, in POR deficiency, endocrine risks; with early airway management, endocrine support and staged craniofacial and orthopaedic surgery, survival and function can be good, though outcomes vary with severity and subtype.
pitfalls: Failing to distinguish POR deficiency and thereby missing a treatable steroidogenic disorder
Overlooking maternal azole exposure as a cause of a phenocopy
Underestimating the neonatal airway risk from combined choanal and midface anomalies
Not evaluating genital and adrenal status when steroid synthesis may be affected
